newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Cricket - Lara steps into more controversy.
newsitem.headline: Cricket - Lara steps into more controversy.

text.p: West Indies officials queried the dismissal of Brian Lara after their star batsman finally found form on the tour of Australia, scoring 86 in a match against Victoria on Friday.
Lara was given out hit wicket after fending off a rising delivery from pace bowler David Saker and setting off for two runs midway through the second day of the four-day match.
His dismissal overshadowed an improved performance by West Indies, who reached 312 for five at the close in response to Victoria's first innings total of 354.
Victorian players appealed to on-field umpires Bob Stratford and Bill Sheahan when Lara, who had watched his shot fly over the slips cordon, started running.

Stratford, standing at square leg, referred the appeals to third umpire Geoff Morrow and Morrow gave Lara out after watching television replays which indicated the 27-year-old left-hander had trodden on his wicket when he started running.

The decision sparked a wave of questions from West Indies players and team management. Wicketkeeper Junior Murray, who is not playing in the match, came on to the field as Lara walked off and questioned the umpires about the dismissal.

Team coach Malcolm Marshall came on to the field 30 minutes later as the players left for tea and also asked for an explanation of the ruling. Team officials were not immediately available for comment.

Lara's dismissal came under section A of Law 35 of the Laws of Cricket, which states that a batsman is out if he breaks his wicket "...in setting off for his first run, immediately after playing, or playing at, the ball".
Lara had appeared on course for his first century on tour after racing from 43 to 86 in 22 balls. He hit 33 from two overs by leg-spinner Brad Stacey, including eight fours and a single.
Jimmy Adams was 43 not out at the close and wicketkeeper Courtney Browne 19. Opener Sherwin Campbell had earlier got the innings off to a good start with a brisk 80.
Lara had scored just 374 runs at an average of 26.7 on tour before the Victoria match.

Lara's poor form mirrored some dismal performances by West Indies during a losing streak of seven matches, including heavy losses in the first two tests against Australia and in the first two matches of the World Series limited overs tournament.
He was reprimanded by team officials after storming into the Australian dressing room to protest his dismissal during the second test.
